query: For the paper "Predicting the Role of Political Trolls in Social Media" (arXiv: 1910.02001), answer this question: Do they only look at tweets?

drafts:
Yes — they only look at tweets.

The authors state they do not have access to user attributes, since the users were banned from Twitter and their accounts suspended, and "we only have access to their tweets thanks to the 'IRA Russian Trolls' dataset" [1]. Each user is represented as a collection of their tweets [4], with the main dataset containing 2,973,371 tweets by 2,848 Twitter users linked to the Russian Internet Research Agency [10]. Even their graph-based approach (the U2M user-to-mentioned-user graph with node2vec) is derived from tweet content, as an edge (u, v) exists if user u mentions user v in their tweets [2].

requirements.reason: 答案明确回应了问题：作者只看推文。引用[1]直接说明作者无法访问用户属性、只有IRA Russian Trolls数据集中的推文；[4]说明每个用户仅由其推文集合表示；[10]给出主数据集为2848个用户的2973371条推文，数字与原文一致；[2]说明图特征也源自推文中的提及，进一步支持'只看推文'的结论。所有引用均为原文连续片段，无多余未支持断言。

citations.quote: For our experi- ments, we use node2vec, as we do not have ac- cess to user attributes: the users have been banned from Twitter, their accounts were suspended, and we only have access to their tweets thanks to the “IRA Russian Trolls” dataset.

We build an undirected User-to-Mentioned-User (U2M) graph, where the nodes are users, and there is an edge (u, v) between two nodes if user u men- tions user v in their tweets (i.e., u has authored a tweet that contains “@v” ).
Given a set of known political troll users (each user being represented as a collection of their tweets), we aim to detect their role: left, right, or news feed.
Our main dataset contains 2 973 371 tweets by 2848 Twitter users, which the US House In- telligence Committee has linked to the Russian Internet Research Agency (IRA).

cited_sources.text: For our experi- ments, we use node2vec, as we do not have ac- cess to user attributes: the users have been banned from Twitter, their accounts were suspended, and we only have access to their tweets thanks to the “IRA Russian Trolls” dataset.

3.1.2 U2M We build an undirected User-to-Mentioned-User (U2M) graph, where the nodes are users, and there is an edge (u, v) between two nodes if user u men- tions user v in their tweets (i.e., u has authored a tweet that contains “@v” ). We run node2vec on this graph and we extract the embeddings for the users. As we are interested only in the troll users, we ignore the embeddings of users who are only mentioned by other trolls.

3 Method Given a set of known political troll users (each user being represented as a collection of their tweets), we aim to detect their role: left, right, or news feed. Linvill and Warren (2018) describe these roles as follows: Right Trolls spread nativist and right-leaning populist messages. Such trolls support the candi- dacy and Presidency of Donald Trump and den- igrate the Democratic Party; moreover, they of- ten send divisive messages about mainstream and moderate Republicans.
4.1 IRA Russian Troll Tweets Our main dataset contains 2 973 371 tweets by 2848 Twitter users, which the US House In- telligence Committee has linked to the Russian Internet Research Agency (IRA).
